referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A sealed rotomoulded shell: nothing opens, turns or swings, the cap is moulded shut, nothing attaches -- linking is done by placing the next unit -- so one root pivot and zero sockets. Reuse density is the point, so the draw-call ceiling is the design constraint. Expressway works and lane closures in interlocked runs of twenty. Faded orange, chalky where the sun has been, tyre scuffs low on the faces, stripes scratched.

reasoning: ONE section -- a 0.10 lip, a taper to half-depth 0.14 at 0.36 and 0.11 at 0.56, a vertical top bar -- extruded 1.02 m along X, with four interlock lugs, a socket mouth, a raised top bar, a cap in two cylinders, four stripe plates and four foot notches, merged on one material: ONE draw call of 2.
One material of two: orange plastic as a vertex colour on white, stripes and cap as vertex colours, scuffs as a grime canvas.
No repetition system: four stripes and four notches are boxes in one merge.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the tapered orange shell with two white stripes on each face, a black cap and the lugs; the section is one extruded polygon and the stripes are plates tilted to the face angle so they read as printed on the slope from every azimuth.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 1.20 x 0.80 x 0.50 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=2000 triangles, <=2 draw calls, <=2 materials, <=4 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/orange.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.880. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-orange (0.88) at #de8060 sd 8 (a lit upper face) and region-scuff at #cb7356; carried at #d9622e as a vertex colour on a WHITE material, stripes #e6e2da off region-stripe #d47251 (a stripe in orange bounce), cap #2a2a2a.
Textureless as DECLARED: a 256 px grime canvas after construction, wash (0.45/0.42/0.40) at 0.55 over the bottom 35%.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

reviewHistory.summary: Form refinement: stripes tilted to the slope, socket mouth, top bar, cap, notches.

Base of the barrier measured at saturation 0.76-0.80 against the plate 0.30: pure orange, only shaded. A multiply cannot desaturate, so the shell was re-based to the per-channel maximum of clean orange and road grime and the tile paints both back.

STRIPE authored at #e6e2ff to survive the tile base fill CLIPPED in blue and the reflective bands rendered CREAM. Scaled to #c1beff so the ratio survives the 0.719 blue factor and lands neutral at (193,190,183).

reviewHistory.summary: Material pass, ENVELOPE RE-BASED. Measured over matched bands: at 0.20-0.45 of the silhouette the plate reads #cf7d62, luma 146 at saturation 0.53, and the build read 155 at 0.60 -- the BODY was already right. At 0.75-0.97 the plate reads #947367, luma 123 at saturation 0.30, and the build read 97 at 0.80: still pure orange, only shaded. That is road grime, and a canvas tile is a MULTIPLY -- it can take the luma down but it CANNOT take the saturation down, because desaturating means raising the smallest channel and multiply only lowers. The harness transfer was probed per channel off two known tones, inverted for the plate grimy #947367, and the shell re-based: clean orange (217,98,46), grime (154,73,64), envelope the per-channel max (217,98,64) = #d96240. The grime is HIGHER IN BLUE than the orange, which is precisely why one vertex colour could not carry both.

reviewHistory.summary: Surface pass: the grime canvas now carries a base fill (the clean orange painted back out of the envelope), a road-grime band over the bottom third, 64 blotches, 16 streaks, and 26 TYRE RUBS -- long near-black smears low on both faces, which is a different colour and a different shape from anything weather does and which the plate has plainly. `base` and `rubs` are new options on grimeTile, both defaulted off; verified byte-identical on concrete-jersey-barrier at max |diff| 0 over the geometry AND mean |diff| 0.0000 max 0 over the rendered frame.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the medium class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

materials.note: plastic only: 1 of 2; stripes and cap are vertex colours.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 316 of 2,000: one 14-point extrusion, thirteen boxes, two cylinders.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: An extruded section along X; boxes for lugs, stripes, notches and the top bar; cylinders for the cap.
No InstancedMesh. In a scene the HOST instances the whole barrier along a run.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
The material is declared textureless. One 256 px grime canvas after construction, 0.25 MB.
